originalTitle: Asian stocks rise as tech rebound, easing U.S. trade concerns lift sentiment
summary: Investing.com -- Most Asian stocks rose on Friday as technology shares extended their recovery and investors took some comfort from easing concerns over U.S. trade tensions, although uncertainty surrounding the artificial-intelligence investment cycle continued to limit risk appetite.
content:
Investing.com -- Most Asian stocks rose on Friday as technology shares extended their recovery and investors took some comfort from easing concerns over U.S. trade tensions, although uncertainty surrounding the artificial-intelligence investment cycle continued to limit risk appetite.

U.S. cash markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving, with Wall Street set to resume trading in a shortened session on Friday. A late recovery in U.S. equities on Wednesday helped stabilise sentiment, while buyers stepped in across Asian technology shares ahead of the holiday break.

Treasury yields resumed their advance as demand for safe-haven assets eased. The 10-year U.S. yield rose five basis points to 4.9%. Nasdaq 100 futures jumped 2.2% and S&P 500 futures gained 1.4% in Asian trade.

Markets are pricing in a 99% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December, although expectations of a larger half-point move have faded.

Oil headed for its first weekly advance in four weeks as attacks on Middle Eastern energy infrastructure and tankers raised concerns over supply disruptions. Brent crude slipped 0.4% to $96.14 a barrel but remained up 3.9% for the week, while monthly losses stood at around 18%.

Asian markets recover, but November losses remain substantial

South Korea's KOSPI gained 3%, Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 1.5% and Taiwan's Weighted Index added 0.8%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng advanced 0.5%, while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 climbed 0.7%.

MSCI's broadest Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan edged up 0.5%, leaving it 1.9% higher for the week but still down 8.2% for November. Japan's Nikkei added 2.7% for the week, although it remained down 8.4% for the month.

South Korea's benchmark recovered around 2% on Friday but remained 16% lower for November, while Taiwan's index was down about 15% this month.

Japan's November core inflation accelerated to 2.9% year-on-year, its fastest pace in 16 months, from 2.6% in October. The reading remained above the Bank of Japan's 2% target for a third consecutive month, strengthening expectations of a possible interest-rate increase at its December 18 meeting.

The Bank of Korea also raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 3.25% on Thursday and upgraded its 2027 growth forecast to 4.1%, citing stronger economic activity and semiconductor demand.

New Zealand's NZX 50 was marginally higher after final election results left parliament without a clear majority. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party secured 40 seats against Labour's 36, leaving the seven-seat centrist Opportunity Party pivotal to government formation.

Chipmakers rebound as corporate developments drive individual stocks

South Korean semiconductor shares advanced, with SK Hynix rising 2.9% and Samsung Electronics gaining 3.6%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. added 1.2%, while Foxconn rose 1.3%.

Japan's Kioxia climbed 6.5%, recovering some ground after losing more than 40% this month on concerns over the sustainability of AI-driven memory demand.

Japan Tobacco gained 3.6% after Bloomberg reported it was considering joining a partner in a potential takeover of British cigarette maker Imperial Brands.

Australia's WiseTech Global surged 16.7% to A$54.61, its highest level since February 4, after management expressed confidence in meeting its full-year revenue guidance.

Nvidia remained a source of uncertainty after S&P Global placed its credit rating on negative watch over governance concerns.

The company also reportedly instructed manufacturing partners to suspend shipments of servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia amid tighter U.S. export controls, the Financial Times reported.

chineseTitle: 科技股反弹，亚洲股市上涨，美国贸易担忧缓解提振市场情绪
chineseSummary: Investing.com——周五大多数亚洲股市上涨，科技股延续复苏势头，投资者因美国贸易紧张局势的担忧缓解而得到一些安慰，尽管人工智能投资周期的不确定性继续限制风险偏好。
chineseContent:
Investing.com——周五大多数亚洲股市上涨，科技股延续复苏势头，投资者因美国贸易紧张局势的担忧缓解而得到一些安慰，尽管人工智能投资周期的不确定性继续限制风险偏好。

美国现货市场周四因感恩节休市，华尔街将于周五在缩短的交易时间内恢复交易。周三美国股市后期的复苏有助于稳定市场情绪，而买家在假期前介入亚洲科技股。

随着避险资产需求放缓，美国国债收益率恢复上涨。美国10年期国债收益率上涨5个基点至4.9%。在亚洲交易中，纳斯达克 100 指数期货上涨 2.2%，标准普尔 500 指数期货上涨 1.4%。

市场预计美联储 12 月加息 25 个基点的可能性为 99%，尽管对更大幅度加息 0.5 个基点的预期已经消退。

由于中东能源基础设施和油轮遇袭引发了人们对供应中断的担忧，油价四个星期以来首次出现周度上涨。布伦特原油下跌 0.4% 至每桶 96.14 美元，但本周仍上涨 3.9%，而月度跌幅约为 18%。

亚洲市场复苏，但 11 月跌幅依然巨大

韩国综合股价指数上涨 3%，日本日经 225 指数上涨 1.5%，台湾加权指数上涨 0.8%。香港恒生指数上涨 0.5%，澳大利亚 S&P/ASX 200 指数上涨 0.7%。

摩根士丹利资本国际（MSCI）最广泛的亚太指数（不包括日本）小幅上涨 0.5%，本周上涨 1.9%，但 11 月份仍下跌 8.2%。日本日经指数本周上涨 2.7%，但本月仍下跌 8.4%。

韩国基准指数周五回升约 2%，但 11 月份仍下跌 16%，而台湾指数本月下跌约 15%。

日本 11 月核心通胀率同比加速至 2.9%，为 16 个月来最快增速，高于 10 月的 2.6%。该数据连续第三个月高于日本央行 2% 的目标，增强了人们对 12 月 18 日会议可能加息的预期。

韩国央行周四还将基准利率上调 25 个基点至 3.25%，并将 2027 年增长预测上调至 4.1%，理由是经济活动和半导体需求更加强劲。

最终选举结果导致新西兰议会没有获得明显多数席位，新西兰 NZX 50 指数小幅走高。总理克里斯托弗·卢克森 (Christopher Luxon) 领导的国家党 (National Party) 赢得了 40 个席位，而工党 (Labour) 则获得了 36 个席位，这使得拥有 7 个席位的中间派机会党 (Opportunity Party) 对政府组建至关重要。

随着企业发展带动个股，芯片制造商反弹

韩国半导体股价上涨，SK 海力士上涨 2.9%，三星电子上涨 3.6%。台积电上涨 1.2%，富士康上涨 1.3%。

日本铠侠 (Kioxia) 上涨 6.5%，在本月因人工智能驱动的内存需求可持续性而下跌超过 40% 后收复部分失地。

据彭博社报道，日本烟草公司正在考虑与合作伙伴一起收购英国卷烟制造商帝国品牌，该公司股价上涨 3.6%。

在管理层表示有信心实现全年收入指引后，澳大利亚慧咨环球股价飙升 16.7%，至 54.61 澳元，为 2 月 4 日以来的最高水平。

在标普全球将其信用评级置于出于治理担忧的负面观察之后，英伟达仍然是不确定性的来源。

据英国《金融时报》报道，由于美国出口管制收紧，该公司还指示制造合作伙伴暂停向马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和印度尼西亚运送包含其芯片的服务器。
